meta.notes: Torah #109 has exactly ONE bechina edge in the dataset (id 1795): נה והאנחה ↔ מיתה בגוף ונפש. This yields a single 2-node connected component. The remaining 4 edges for this Torah are all eitza type. The Torah's content is much richer in bechina language than the dataset captures — the source text contains at least 3 additional explicit bechina pairs not yet in the dataset. The single dataset package below is supplemented by source-text-derived packages in the gap analysis. The Torah's teaching: the breath-vapor (הבל) of sighing IS the rope (חבל) that connects the soul to its root — for good or evil. The sigh IS a mini-death (מיתה) that severs one connection and establishes another. Two structural rope-domains (קדושה / טומאה) form a classic good/evil mirror.

packages.label: נֹּהַּ וְהָאֲנָחָה — הָאֲנָחָה כְּמִיתָה
packages.label_en: The Sigh as Death — Groaning and the Death-Process
packages.reason: This 2-node component is the only connected component in the bechina subgraph for Torah #109. The Rebbe establishes an explicit bechina: 'הַנֹּהַּ וְהָאֲנָחָה הוּא בְּחִינַת מִיתָה בְּגוּף וָנֶפֶשׁ' — the groaning and sighing IS a bechina of death in body and soul. The shared essential nature is the process of vital-force gathering and then releasing/expiring. The Rebbe supports this from Berakhot 58b ('a sigh breaks a person's body') for the bodily dimension, and from Tehillim 104:29 ('when You gather their spirit, they expire') for the soul dimension. Polarity is neutral because this death-process operates in BOTH directions: sighing over sins leads to dying away from evil and attaching to holiness; sighing over good leads to dying away from holiness and attaching to impurity. The sigh-as-death is the mechanism that can go either way — it is the pivot of the entire Torah. The node with greatest centrality-to-teaching is נה והאנחה (groaning and sighing), which is the active agent; מיתה בגוף ונפש describes its essential nature.
merge_notes: This 2-node component is the only component in the dataset. The source-text gap analysis (see additions file) reveals two additional bechina clusters: (1) הבל / חבל הנשמה / תוסף רוחם — the breath as a soul-connecting rope; (2) חבל דקדשה / חבל דטמאה — the two opposing rope-domains. These would constitute Package 2 (good) and Package 3 (evil) respectively. See torah_109_additions.json and torah_109_new_packages.json.

good_evil_mirror.note: This neutral package sits at the center of the Torah's good/evil mirror. The 'death' enacted by the sigh can sever connection to evil (→ good outcome) or sever connection to good (→ evil outcome). The sigh itself is the pivot, not polarized. The two rope-clusters (חבל דקדשה / חבל דטמאה) ARE the polar mirror — see gap analysis.

good_evil_mirror_structure.description: Torah #109 has a clean binary good/evil mirror, but it is expressed through the TWO ROPE domains rather than through the single dataset-captured bechina. The soul is always connected to exactly one of two ropes: חבל דקדושה (the holy rope) or חבל דטומאה (the impurity rope). These two ropes are the exact structural mirror. The sigh (Package 1, neutral) is the mechanism of switching: one sigh severs connection to one rope and establishes connection to the other. The Torah's argument is: the penitent sinner's sigh severs him from the evil rope and attaches him to the holy rope; the righteous person's mournful sigh over his past good can (Heaven forbid) sever him from the holy rope and attach him to the evil rope.
